name: Toronto
tagline: Canada's big, multicultural city on the lake
summary: Canada's largest city sits on Lake Ontario, with the CN Tower over a skyline of glass towers. Half its people were born abroad, so its neighbourhoods and food come from all over the world, and Niagara Falls is an easy day trip.
seasonNote: June to September is warm, with festivals almost every weekend, including the film festival (TIFF) in September. October brings autumn colours. Winters are cold and snowy, from December to March.
arrival: Pearson Airport is 25 minutes from Union Station on the UP Express train. Billy Bishop Airport on the islands has flights from nearby cities, and trains run from Montreal (about 5 hours).
gettingAround: The TTC subway, streetcars and buses use one fare with a Presto card or a tap of your bank card; ferries cross to the islands.
cashTip: Cards and tap payments work everywhere; tip 15 to 20 percent in restaurants.
foodTip: Peameal bacon sandwiches, butter tarts, Caribbean roti and dim sum, plus food from almost every country.
buyTip: Maple syrup, Canadian whisky, Indigenous art and ice wine.
baseArea: Downtown near Union Station, or the Annex

items.name: CN Tower
items.summary: A 553 m tower with a glass floor and an outdoor EdgeWalk around the top.
items.expect: Timed tickets; queues at weekends.
items.tip: Go at sunset to see the city both by day and lit up.

items.name: Royal Ontario Museum
items.summary: Canada's largest museum, from dinosaurs to world cultures, behind a crystal-shaped entrance.
items.expect: Allow at least half a day.
items.tip: Start with the dinosaur gallery.

items.name: Toronto Islands
items.summary: A car-free chain of islands with beaches, bike paths and skyline views.
items.expect: A 15-minute ferry from the Jack Layton terminal.
items.tip: Take the ferry to Ward's Island and walk back along the boardwalk.
items.why: The best skyline view in the city.

items.name: Distillery District
items.summary: Victorian brick distillery buildings turned into galleries, cafés and shops.
items.expect: Pedestrian-only; Christmas market in December.
items.tip: Visit in the evening when it's lit.

items.name: Art Gallery of Ontario
items.summary: A major gallery redesigned by Frank Gehry, with Canadian and Indigenous art.
items.expect: Free on Wednesday evenings.
items.tip: See the Group of Seven paintings.

items.name: Kensington Market
items.summary: A bohemian neighbourhood of vintage shops, street art and food from everywhere.
items.expect: Car-free on some summer Sundays.
items.tip: Graze from stall to stall.

items.name: Niagara Falls
items.summary: The thundering Horseshoe Falls, seen up close from a boat.
items.expect: About 1.5 hours by car or train; the boats run from spring to autumn.
items.tip: Take the boat into the mist, then visit Niagara-on-the-Lake for wine.
items.why: One of the world's great waterfalls.

items.name: Peameal bacon sandwich
items.summary: Thick slices of cornmeal-crusted back bacon in a bun, a Toronto original.
items.expect: At the famous St. Lawrence Market.
items.tip: Get there before noon on Saturday.

items.name: Butter tarts
items.summary: Small pastry tarts with a gooey butter, sugar and syrup filling.
items.expect: Sold in bakeries everywhere.
items.tip: Try one with and one without raisins.

items.name: Caribbean roti
items.summary: Flatbread wrapped around curried goat, chicken or chickpeas.
items.expect: Small shops along Eglinton Avenue West.
items.tip: Order a goat roti with hot sauce.

name: Montreal
tagline: French North America with a festival in every season
summary: Montreal is the world's second-largest French-speaking city, on an island in the St Lawrence. Its cobbled old town, the glowing Notre-Dame Basilica and Mount Royal park sit beside lively neighbourhoods, and it's famous for bagels, smoked meat, poutine and summer festivals.
seasonNote: June to August is festival season, led by the Jazz Festival and Just for Laughs. September and October bring autumn colours. Winters are long and very cold, but the city has an underground network and winter festivals.
arrival: Montréal–Trudeau Airport is 30 to 45 minutes from downtown by the 747 bus or taxi. Trains run from Toronto (about 5 hours), Quebec City (3 hours) and New York (11 hours).
gettingAround: The metro is quick and simple; BIXI bikes are everywhere in summer, and the old town is walkable.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; tip 15 to 20 percent. French is the main language, but most people also speak English.
foodTip: Poutine, wood-fired bagels, smoked meat sandwiches and maple treats.
buyTip: Maple syrup, ice cider, Quebec cheese and local designer clothes.

connections.note: VIA Rail trains or a 75-minute flight.

items.name: Old Montreal
items.summary: Cobbled streets, 18th-century stone houses and the Old Port on the river.
items.expect: Busy in summer; romantic in winter lights.
items.tip: Walk Rue Saint-Paul and finish at the Old Port.
items.why: The French heart of the city.

items.name: Notre-Dame Basilica
items.summary: A Gothic Revival church with a deep-blue, gold-starred interior.
items.expect: An entry fee; the AURA light show runs in the evenings.
items.tip: Book the AURA show.
items.why: One of North America's most beautiful churches.

items.name: Mount Royal
items.summary: The park on the mountain the city is named for, with a lookout over downtown.
items.expect: A 30-minute walk up from downtown.
items.tip: Visit the Kondiaronk lookout at sunset; on summer Sundays join the Tam-Tams drum gathering.

items.name: Saint Joseph's Oratory
items.summary: Canada's largest church, a domed shrine on the slope of Mount Royal.
items.expect: Free entry; pilgrims climb the stairs on their knees.
items.tip: Go up to the dome observatory.

items.name: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts
items.summary: Canada's oldest art museum, with Quebec, Canadian and world art.
items.expect: Five pavilions; free for under-21s.
items.tip: See the Quebec and Canadian art pavilion.

items.name: Le Plateau and Mile End
items.summary: Colourful houses with winding outside staircases, cafés and boutiques.
items.expect: Best explored on foot or by bike.
items.tip: Walk Rue Saint-Denis, then Mile End's bagel shops.

items.name: Jean-Talon Market
items.summary: One of North America's biggest open-air markets, full of Quebec produce.
items.expect: Open daily; best in late summer and autumn.
items.tip: Taste maple products and Quebec cheeses.

items.name: Quebec City
items.summary: The walled old town of Quebec, with the Château Frontenac over the river.
items.expect: About 3 hours by train or car.
items.tip: Stay overnight if you can.
items.why: North America's only walled city north of Mexico.

items.name: Poutine
items.summary: Fries topped with cheese curds and gravy.
items.expect: Late-night favourite.
items.tip: Try the classic before any fancy versions.

items.name: Montreal bagels
items.summary: Small, sweet, wood-fired bagels boiled in honey water.
items.expect: Shops open 24 hours.
items.tip: Get them hot from St-Viateur or Fairmount.

items.name: Smoked meat sandwich
items.summary: Spiced, smoked beef brisket piled on rye bread with mustard.
items.expect: There's usually a queue at the famous deli.
items.tip: Order it 'medium' fat.

name: Melbourne
summary: Melbourne is Australia's culture capital, known for hidden laneway cafés and street art, great galleries and a passion for sport at the MCG. It's the start of the Great Ocean Road, and Phillip Island's little penguins come ashore nearby every evening.
seasonNote: March to May and October to December are mild and pleasant. Summer (January and February) can be very hot. Winter is cool and grey. The weather changes fast, so 'four seasons in one day' is a local joke.
arrival: Melbourne Airport is 30 minutes from the city by SkyBus. Flights from Sydney take about 1.5 hours; the overnight ferry runs to Tasmania.
gettingAround: Trams are free inside the city centre; tap on with a myki card outside it.
cashTip: Cards and tap payments work almost everywhere; tipping isn't expected.
foodTip: Flat whites, brunch, Vietnamese and Greek food, Italian on Lygon Street, and dumplings in Chinatown.
buyTip: Australian wine, design from local makers, Aboriginal art and Tim Tams.

connections.note: One of the world's busiest air routes.

items.name: Hosier Lane and the laneways
items.summary: Graffiti-covered lanes and hidden arcades full of tiny cafés.
items.expect: Free; the art changes every week.
items.tip: Walk from Hosier Lane to Degraves Street and the Block Arcade.

items.name: Federation Square
items.summary: A public square of angular buildings with galleries and big screens.
items.expect: Home of ACMI, the screen museum.
items.tip: Visit ACMI; it's free.

items.name: National Gallery of Victoria
items.summary: Australia's oldest and most visited gallery, with a stained-glass ceiling hall.
items.expect: The permanent collection is free.
items.tip: Lie on the floor of the Great Hall to see the glass ceiling.

items.name: Queen Victoria Market
items.summary: A huge 19th-century market of produce, delis and souvenirs.
items.expect: Closed Mondays and Wednesdays; a night market in summer.
items.tip: Go to the Wednesday summer night market.

items.name: Royal Botanic Gardens
items.summary: Rolling lawns, lakes and plants from around the world.
items.expect: Free; a short walk from the city.
items.tip: Walk the 'Tan' track around the gardens.
items.why: One of the world's great gardens.

items.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
items.summary: A 100,000-seat stadium for cricket in summer and Aussie rules football in winter.
items.expect: Tours on non-match days.
items.tip: See a game if you can.

items.name: St Kilda
items.summary: A seaside suburb with a pier, Luna Park and cake shops.
items.expect: Little penguins live at the end of the pier.
items.tip: Go to the pier at dusk to see the penguins.

items.name: Great Ocean Road and Twelve Apostles
items.summary: A clifftop coastal drive to the limestone stacks of the Twelve Apostles.
items.expect: A very long day trip (12 hours); better over two days.
items.tip: Stay overnight near Apollo Bay or Port Campbell.
items.why: One of the world's great road trips.

items.name: Phillip Island penguin parade
items.summary: Thousands of little penguins waddle ashore at sunset.
items.expect: About 2 hours by car; no photos at the parade.
items.tip: Book the viewing platform ahead.

items.name: Flat white and brunch
items.summary: Melbourne's serious coffee culture and big brunches.
items.expect: Cafés open early and close mid-afternoon.
items.tip: Try smashed avocado on toast.
items.why: Coffee is a way of life here.

items.name: Lygon Street Italian
items.summary: Melbourne's Little Italy, with pasta, pizza and espresso bars.
items.expect: Busy restaurants with outdoor tables.
items.tip: Finish with gelato.

items.name: Chinatown dumplings
items.summary: Dumplings and noodles in one of the Western world's oldest Chinatowns.
items.expect: Cheap and quick.
items.tip: Order xiao long bao.

name: Auckland
tagline: The city of sails between two harbours
summary: New Zealand's largest city sits on a narrow strip between two harbours, dotted with volcanic cones. It has the country's best Māori and Pacific collections, ferries to vineyard islands like Waiheke, and wild black-sand surf beaches less than an hour away.
seasonNote: December to March is summer, warm and busy. Spring and autumn are mild. Winter (June to August) is wet but rarely cold.
arrival: Auckland Airport is 40 minutes from the city by SkyDrop bus or car. Flights from Sydney take about 3 hours; domestic flights reach Queenstown and Wellington in under 2 hours.
gettingAround: Ferries, buses and trains share the AT HOP card; rent a car for beaches and day trips.
cashTip: Cards and tap payments work everywhere; tipping isn't expected.
foodTip: Fish and chips on the beach, pavlova, a hāngī earth-oven meal and Waiheke wine.
buyTip: Pounamu (greenstone), merino wool, mānuka honey and Māori carvings from reputable makers.

items.name: Sky Tower
items.summary: A 328 m tower with views over both harbours, plus SkyWalk and SkyJump.
items.expect: Timed tickets; clear days are best.
items.tip: Go at sunset.

items.name: Auckland War Memorial Museum
items.summary: A grand museum with world-class Māori and Pacific treasures and a daily cultural performance.
items.expect: Free for Aucklanders; a fee for visitors.
items.tip: See the Māori cultural performance.
items.why: The best introduction to New Zealand.

items.name: Waiheke Island
items.summary: Vineyards, olive groves and beaches, 40 minutes by ferry.
items.expect: Hop-on bus or e-bike between wineries.
items.tip: Book a winery lunch.

items.name: Maungawhau / Mount Eden
items.summary: A grassy volcanic cone with a deep crater and 360-degree city views.
items.expect: Free; a 20-minute walk up.
items.tip: Go at sunrise.
items.why: The highest volcano in the city.

items.name: Rangitoto Island
items.summary: The city's youngest volcano, with lava fields and a summit walk.
items.expect: 25 minutes by ferry; no shops on the island.
items.tip: Bring water and food, and catch the last ferry.

items.name: Viaduct Harbour
items.summary: A waterfront of yachts, restaurants and the Maritime Museum.
items.expect: Lively in the evening.
items.tip: Take a harbour sailing trip.

items.name: Piha Beach
items.summary: A wild black-sand surf beach below Lion Rock.
items.expect: About 45 minutes by car; dangerous rips.
items.tip: Swim only between the lifeguard flags.

items.name: Hobbiton Movie Set
items.summary: The Shire film set, with hobbit holes and the Green Dragon inn.
items.expect: Guided tours only; about 2 hours each way by road.
items.tip: Book ahead and combine with Rotorua.

items.name: Fish and chips
items.summary: Battered fresh fish and chunky chips wrapped in paper.
items.expect: Best eaten on the beach.
items.tip: Ask for local snapper or tarakihi.

items.name: Pavlova
items.summary: A meringue cake with a crisp shell, soft centre, cream and fruit.
items.expect: Kiwis and Australians both claim it.
items.tip: Try it with kiwifruit.

items.name: Hāngī
items.summary: Meat and vegetables slow-cooked in a Māori earth oven.
items.expect: Usually part of a cultural evening or market.
items.tip: Look for hāngī at weekend markets.

name: Punta Cana
summary: On the Dominican Republic's eastern tip, Punta Cana is a long coast of white sand, palms and turquoise water lined with resorts. Beyond the beach there are boat trips to Saona Island, cenotes, and the colonial capital Santo Domingo a few hours away.
seasonNote: December to April is dry and sunny, and the busiest. May to November is hotter and wetter; hurricane season peaks from August to October. Sargassum seaweed can wash up in summer.
arrival: Punta Cana International Airport is 15 to 30 minutes from most resorts, with direct flights from North America and Europe. Fill in the free e-Ticket entry form before you fly.
gettingAround: Resorts arrange transfers; use official taxis (agree the fare first) or a car with driver for trips.
cashTip: US dollars are widely accepted, but you'll get better prices in pesos; drink bottled water, not tap water.
foodTip: La bandera (rice, beans and meat), mangú for breakfast, fresh fish and mamajuana.
buyTip: Larimar jewellery, amber, cigars, coffee and cacao.

items.name: Bávaro Beach
items.summary: Kilometres of soft white sand and calm, clear water behind a reef.
items.expect: Public access between resorts.
items.tip: Walk the beach at sunrise.

items.name: Macao Beach
items.summary: A wilder, undeveloped beach with surf and local food shacks.
items.expect: Surf schools rent boards.
items.tip: Take a surf lesson.

items.name: Juanillo Beach
items.summary: A long, quiet beach of white sand in the Cap Cana estate.
items.expect: Upmarket beach clubs.
items.tip: Visit on a weekday.
items.why: One of the island's most beautiful beaches.

items.name: Hoyo Azul cenote
items.summary: A turquoise freshwater pool at the foot of a cliff, inside an adventure park.
items.expect: Entry through the park; the water is cold and clear.
items.tip: Go early before groups arrive.

items.name: Indigenous Eyes Ecological Reserve
items.summary: Freshwater lagoons in a coastal forest reserve.
items.expect: Guided walks and swimming in the lagoons.
items.tip: Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

items.name: Saona Island
items.summary: A national-park island of palm beaches and a shallow natural pool with starfish.
items.expect: A full-day boat trip; don't pick up the starfish.
items.tip: Choose a smaller-group tour.

items.name: Altos de Chavón
items.summary: A replica Mediterranean village over the Chavón river, with an amphitheatre.
items.expect: About 1.5 hours by car.
items.tip: Combine it with a Saona trip from La Romana.

items.name: La bandera
items.summary: Rice, red beans and stewed meat, the Dominican daily lunch.
items.expect: Served at local comedores.
items.tip: Try it outside the resorts.

items.name: Mangú breakfast
items.summary: Mashed green plantains with fried cheese, salami and eggs, called 'los tres golpes'.
items.expect: Breakfast staple.
items.tip: Ask for pickled red onion on top.

items.name: Fresh fish at the beach
items.summary: Whole fried fish with tostones at a beach shack.
items.expect: Priced by size.
items.tip: Agree the price first.

name: Sharm El Sheikh
tagline: Red Sea reefs at the foot of Sinai
summary: On the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, Sharm El Sheikh is a resort town with some of the world's best coral reefs just offshore. Divers and snorkellers head to Ras Mohammed and the Straits of Tiran, and night trips climb Mount Sinai for sunrise above Saint Catherine's Monastery.
seasonNote: March to May and October to November are warm with comfortable sea temperatures. Summer is very hot; winter evenings are cool, though the sea stays swimmable.
arrival: Check your government's travel advice first: it usually treats the South Sinai resorts differently from North Sinai, where many advise against all travel. Sharm El Sheikh Airport is 15 minutes from Naama Bay, with flights from Cairo (1 hour) and Europe. Visitors staying only in South Sinai resorts can get a free Sinai-only entry stamp.
gettingAround: Taxis and hotel transfers; agree taxi fares first. Dive centres collect you from your hotel.
cashTip: Carry Egyptian pounds for markets and tips; euros and US dollars are accepted in many tourist places.
foodTip: Fresh grilled seafood, koshari, ful and falafel, and sweet mint tea with Bedouin hosts.
buyTip: Spices, papyrus, cotton clothes and Bedouin silver.

items.name: Ras Mohammed National Park
items.summary: A protected headland where reef walls drop into the deep blue.
items.expect: Best by boat; also reachable by car for snorkelling from the shore.
items.tip: Book a boat trip to Shark and Yolanda Reef.
items.why: One of the world's top dive sites.

items.name: Straits of Tiran reefs
items.summary: Four coral reefs in the straits between Sinai and Tiran Island.
items.expect: Day boats from Sharm; strong currents.
items.tip: Go on a day boat with snorkel guides.
items.why: Huge coral and shoals of fish.

items.name: Naama Bay
items.summary: A sandy bay with a seafront promenade of cafés, bars and dive shops.
items.expect: Busy at night.
items.tip: Snorkel the house reefs at the edges of the bay.

items.name: Old Market
items.summary: Bazaar lanes of spices, lanterns and cafés around the old town.
items.expect: Bargaining expected.
items.tip: Come in the evening and stay for seafood.

items.name: Al Sahaba Mosque
items.summary: A striking white mosque in Ottoman and Mamluk style beside the Old Market.
items.expect: Visitors may see it from outside; dress modestly if you're allowed inside.
items.tip: See it lit up at night.

items.name: Desert safari and Bedouin camp
items.summary: Quad bikes, camel rides and a Bedouin dinner under the stars.
items.expect: Evening trips from most hotels.
items.tip: Choose a small operator.
items.why: The Sinai desert on your doorstep.

items.name: Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's Monastery
items.summary: A night climb to the summit for sunrise, then the ancient monastery at its foot.
items.expect: About 3 hours each way by road; leaves around 11 pm.
items.tip: Bring warm clothes; it is cold on top.
items.why: Holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims.

items.name: Blue Hole, Dahab
items.summary: A deep sinkhole in the reef, famous with freedivers, near laid-back Dahab.
items.expect: About 1.5 hours by road; snorkel the rim, not the depths.
items.tip: Snorkel the reef edge and lunch in Dahab.

items.name: Grilled seafood
items.summary: Fish and prawns picked from the counter and grilled with rice and salads.
items.expect: Priced by weight.
items.tip: Agree the price first.

items.name: Koshari
items.summary: Rice, lentils, pasta and chickpeas with tomato sauce and fried onions.
items.expect: Cheap and filling.
items.tip: Add the garlic vinegar and chilli.

items.name: Bedouin tea
items.summary: Sweet black tea brewed with desert herbs over a fire.
items.expect: Served at Bedouin camps.
items.tip: Accept the third glass.
